utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I'd like to begin my examination of the witness this afternoon with a few questions in private session, if that would be okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we are now in open session, so we are going to be broadcasting your answers to the public. Can I ask you, do you know when Milan Lukic left Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I had left already. In 1972 I joined the army, and then after that I got a job elsewhere, so I can't tell you when it was that he left Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise Milan Lukic yesterday when you entered the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any difficulty doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic have any relatives that worked in the police, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, maybe some distant relative, three or four times removed, Sreten Lukic, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyone other than Sreten Lukic that you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you familiar with an area of Visegrad known as Zupa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many different villages would you say are in the area known as Zupa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's all the way from Prelovo to the Serbian border, a village called Zenica. That's what we refer to as Zupa. There are quite a number of villages, such as Paocici, Rijeka, Pozarcic, and so forth, all sorts of names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you, sir. I'd like to ask you about your evidence about what happened in Kopito on the 13th to the 15th of June 1992, and I'd like to begin that by asking you to make some -- to look at a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could I ask that the following map be placed on the screen for the witness, and that's ERN 0632-2731.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in a few moments, sir, you'll see a map come up on the screen where you saw photographs yesterday. Once it does come up and you've had a chance to look at it, I'd ask you, do you recognise the area that's depicted in the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we enlarge the lower third of the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise what's depicted in the map, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is this road that we discussed yesterday, Kopito.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender an unmarked version of this map before I ask the witness to make any marks on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P 233, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask the court usher to assist you in making a few marks on the map. I'm going to ask that the pen be set to blue. I kindly ask you not to make any markings until I completely describe what I would like you to mark. If you do that, hopefully the map will help us understand your testimony better. Now, it seems that you've already identified the road between Visegrad and Kopito. Could I ask you to draw a blue line to indicate the road you took from Visegrad to Kopito on the 13th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this map doesn't state where Kopito is. Could I ask you to approximate the location of Kopito by putting a "K" on the approximate location on the road of where Kopito would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It should be somewhere between Sjemec and Borike, around about here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I ask you to put a "K" -- you've drawn a line across that road. Could I ask you to put a "K" next to that line so that we know that is where you intended to mark Kopito.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would object. It appears that he marked on three locations on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is that a "K"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could I ask you to put place a circle around the "K" just so it's clear that it's a "K".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just to deal with Mr. Alarid's point, perhaps he could explain what the first mark is that he made.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, he made two marks in response to my request to mark the road. I'm going to can him to draw a solid line along the entire road. Perhaps that would clear it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask you to draw a continuous solid blue line from the point of Visegrad all the way to the point in Kopito that you've now marked to indicate the road that you took on the 13th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seems you've stopped short of Kopito. If the "K" indicates Kopito, I would ask you to draw the line all the way to where you've marked Kopito.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday in your testimony, you referred to a place known as Tabla. Can I ask you to put a "T" next to the place in the road where Tabla was located. Maybe draw a line across the road as you did with Kopito to indicate the precise location.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it misstates the evidence to the precise location with respect to Kopito. He said approximately here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's noted. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to put a "T" next to the road where -- the approximate location of where Tabla is located.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It should be somewhere between Gornja Lijeska and Donja Lijeska, closer to Donja Lijeska than to Gornja Lijeska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to circle that "T", sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, to help us assist us in making sense of your markings at a later date, am I correct in saying the circle indicating Tabla is the circle that's closer to the town of Visegrad, and the circle for Kopito is the one that's further away from Visegrad. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Tabla is closer to Visegrad than to Kopito.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it your evidence that Commander Tripkovic was killed at Tabla, or is it a different location that I need to ask you to mark?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right at that bend, and Tabla is just by the road there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you to make one more marking in blue. I'm going to ask you to put the initials "ML" with a circle around it to indicate where it was that you saw Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should locate Bikavac first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The question ought to be -- define as to what time he testified to seeing Milan Lukic at several times throughout the 13th to the 15th. So, Your Honour, to be fair to the witness, we should narrow it down in terms of which time period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, if you can be a little more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, perhaps it's not even necessary to mark this. When you stayed overnight with Milan Lukic, that was in Kopito; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We spent two nights together at Kopito.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I don't believe I need to ask you to mark "ML."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that the pen be change to red now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to draw a second line now, and it may very well be right along the lines or in part along the lines that you've just testified that, but I want to see if you can help us with this. If someone were to drive from Visegrad in the direction of Sjemec mountain, could you draw the road that they would take.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same road that I marked in blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You now have a red pen. Could I ask you just -- for the sake of clarity, just draw a red line now right along the blue line from Visegrad to Sjemec mountain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if the a person was then to continue on from Sjemec mountain to the town of Seljani in Rogatica, could you show us the road that they would take from Sjemec mountain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. What was the place that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The place that I'm asking you to draw to is Seljani, and that's S-e-l-j-a-n-e.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have heard of that place, but I don't know where that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Olovo? Do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. I think it's past Sarajevo or in the general Sarajevo area as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay sir. I won't ask you to make any marks for which you're not certain. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And Your Honour, at this time I tender the marked map as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P 234, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if I remember your testimony correctly from yesterday, you said that this was the only combat operation that you were involved in during the course of your military service; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With Milan Lukic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is one of the reasons why you have such a clear memory of it; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's one of the reasons, but the principal reason, I remember this, is this was the first time I had ever seen anything like this, a car on fire, the one in which Vlatko Tripkovic and Novica Savic were incinerated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that on the morning of the 13th, you were working up on the right bank of the Drina doing guard duty in the area of Prelovo, Rujiste. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that your commander came up there in a Lada Niva and told you to get in and that you were going to Kopito to lay an ambush. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. A driver came in a Lada Niva and told the komandir to pick us up and that we should be on our way to the command, but that was all we knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, let me read you a portion of your testimony yesterday that seems to what you're saying now. And this is at transcript 4543. Mr. Ivetic asked you: "Now could you detail for us how it was you came to be involved in this action in the region of Kopito in Visegrad municipality beginning the 13th of June, 1992?" To that question, you answered: "A Lada Niva came, and the commander told me to get in the car and we should go because we needed to go up to Kopito as the Muslim soldiers were passing on the Gorazde-Zepa, Zepa-Gorazde road, and they had the even set fire to some houses up there, and we had to set up an ambush." Do you remember yesterday being asked that question and giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was what we were told at the command. When we arrived at the command, this news was conveyed to us, and not at the same place where our positions were or where I was taking up positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's your evidence today that at the time you were up on guard duty, you were not told what you were being asked to do. It was not until you reached the command in Bikavac that you were told; is that correct? Is that your evidence today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's where we were told where we'd be going next, but while I was guarding that other area down there when they came to pick us up, all they told us at the time was that we would be going to the Bikavac command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did it take you to drive from where you were on guard duty to the command centre at the Bikavac hotel that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 40 to 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you drive through the village of Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Koritnik was on my left. As we drove past on our way from the position to Bikavac, Koritnik would have been on the left side, but we wouldn't pass it in our way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you drive through the village of Greben?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything unusual in the village of Greben that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I could take you to the time in front of the Bikavac hotel. You testified that you saw Milan Lukic in front of the Bikavac hotel when you arrived there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And further, you testified that after you arrived in Visegrad on the 1st of May, you had not seen Milan Lukic until this point in time, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seemed from your evidence yesterday that you were surprised when you saw him there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Surprised? Maybe not surprised, but it had been some time, so I'm not sure if I would call it a surprise, but we hadn't seen each other for some time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask the question in this way: Had anyone told you that Milan Lukic had returned to Visegrad and had taken up arms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, it's your evidence that you returned on the 1st of May, and this is now the 13th of June, six weeks later. It's your evidence that you never saw Milan Lukic in the six weeks between your return and this day, the 13th of June, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you testified about the older Milan Lukic and the younger Milan Lukic. The older Milan Lukic would have been in his late 50s in 1992. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably. He was an elderly person. He had a family, grown-up children. I think he was born in the 1930s, 1935, possibly 1936, but don't hold me to it, give or take a year or two, but he would have been aged about 50 at the time, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So MLD4, would you agree with me that it would not be likely for someone to confuse the older Milan Lukic with the younger Milan Lukic, would it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why don't you ask him whether he would have confused the older Milan Lukic with the younger.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is there any possibility that if you saw both Milan Lukices, that you would possibly confuse one for the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No way, no way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, the older Milan Lukic, was he starting to have some gray in his hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he -- sorry. Was he balding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, back to this mission, the purpose of this mission was, as you told us yesterday, to lay an ambush for some Muslim soldiers you expected to cross the Visegrad-Rogatica road. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Zepa-Gorazde, Gorazde-Zepa, that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was the information you were given were that Muslim soldiers using the road between Gorazde and Zepa would cross over the Visegrad-Rogatica road, and that's where you wanted to lay an ambush; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday in your -- well, at this stage, the road is not blocked. Is that correct? The road from Visegrad to where you were supposed to go on this mission, you had no information that this road was blocked in any way, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We passed through that -- along that road and reached Kopito without any problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the place that you intended to ambush them, yesterday you described it as a path going between Gorazde and Zepa, and I believe you referred to it or that you called it or is commonly referred to as a goat path. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a path that a truck or a bus could drive along?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no. Only a man mounted on a horse or a donkey or on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to take you to the point in time where you're at Kopito. When you arrived at Kopito, you were met by Vlatko Tripkovic, who introduced himself to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the first time you saw him that day was in Kopito; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was not down at the command in the Bikavac hotel in Visegrad town, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that morning when we set out, no, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're sure of that; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm a hundred per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also testified that you met Novica Savic up there at Kopito as well. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The two of them met us up there with two or three other local men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Novica Savic was not down in the Bikavac hotel command earlier in the day, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's not clear for me from your testimony yesterday about the person you referred to as Perica Markovic. Where did you see him for the first time that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that morning in front of the command at Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was in Bikavac, and he travelled up with the group to Kopito?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you then testified that at some point, Tripkovic went to Visegrad sometime on the 13th, and it was sometime after you had arrived in Kopito, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He -- well, Novica Savic deployed us on one side of that road, Tripkovic on the other, and they discussed something with Perica Markovic. Later on, we received an order from Perica who said that he was in charge of the action, and the other two said, We are going to Visegrad for the briefing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present -- were you present when Tripkovic said to the men that he was going to Visegrad for the briefing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We were already deployed. It was Perica Markovic who told us afterwards that Tripkovic and Savic had gone off to Visegrad for the briefing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the communications equipment that Tripkovic had, was that communications equipment that he carried with himself?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. Calls for speculation -- it calls for speculation, and I don't think proper foundation has been laid for this type of question for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to answer the question whether the communications equipment that Tripkovic had was equipment that he carried with himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw Tripkovic with a Motorola, and as for whether he had something in the car, and if he did, what it was, I couldn't say. Because the car was some distance away from us, I did not approach it, nor did I see what's inside it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's your evidence that that was the only radio communications equipment that was present at Kopito at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I saw. I don't know if someone had something else, but I didn't see it if they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it possible that other people who went with you to Kopito had other sets of radio communications equipment?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Calls for speculation and misstates the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ask another question, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it your evidence that on the eve of an important operation in Trivkovic's area of responsibility, that he set out to drive to Visegrad to speak with his superiors rather than to simply talk to with them on the radio that he had with him? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, it misstates the evidence. He stated that his knowledge of this --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, these objections are just meant to coach the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness answer this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your evidence, sir, that, rather than just call up the superiors in Visegrad on the radio, he decided on the eve on an important engagement to drive down there and speak to them in person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At certain times, they held briefings in the command with a Brigade commander, and we did not see this as a big action. It was more like a barricade, if those men came along to stop them and prevent them from passing through there and prevent them from making an incursion as they had done previously in other places and burned down houses. We didn't see this as an important action. We simply saw this as setting up a barricade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you see anyone else in the group that went with you from Bikavac to Kopito with radio equipment? Did you see anyone else with radio equipment?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Asked and answered three times already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see that anyone had radio equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At other military operations that you were engaged in, would it have been common practice to go out into the field to conduct an operation without having radio equipment with you? Is that something that you've seen in other times that you've gone out on engagements?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll object as to relevance and as to this witness -- foundation being laid as to what the common practice was. This witness testified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The objection is baseless.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please answer the question. Were you ever on another operation where you went out to do an engagement in the field and did not carry radio equipment with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When actions are being set up, and I'm repeating that this was a sort of barricade, but when actions were mounted, there were people there who had communications equipment. I, as an ordinary private, never had such equipment, nor did I ever carry it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of the day was Tripkovic killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it might have been between 10 and 11.00, perhaps, around 11, probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the morning or in the -- at night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the morning, about 11 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Tripkovic would have been killed about 10 in the morning of the 13th; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, more like 11.00 in the morning of the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long does it take to get from the Bikavac hotel to Kopito?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection as to foundation. Clarification as to mode of transport.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will you stop these objections which really have no base? It's for the witness to answer the question. If he can't answer it, then he can't answer it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long would it take to get from Bikavac hotel to Kopito?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if you have a passenger car, a small one, maybe 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long was Tripkovic in your presence before you no longer saw him on the day of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe some 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you find out that Commander Tripkovic had been killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We learned that on the 14th from Goran Djeric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Goran Djeric tell you how he learned it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Visegrad and Rogatica Brigades had communications, and from Bikavac you can see the smoke, and you can see the license plate, so they probably observed to see what was happening, and they called up Tripkovic, and he probably didn't respond, but all this is an assumption on my part. Probably he failed to respond and then they contacted the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it your evidence that from the Bikavac command centre, it would be possible to read the license plate of the car where -- the burnt car where Tripkovic was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. But they could see the flames. They couldn't maybe even tell what sort of car it was, but they would be able to see the flames of the car burning, and probably they would have heard shooting as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is the location where Tripkovic was killed to Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As the crow flies, maybe less than 2 kilometers uphill, less than 2 kilometers as the crow flies, and along the road, 5 or 6 kilometers, because it's a winding road. It winds is lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that you would be able to discern a car from Bikavac hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no. I said maybe they wouldn't be able to discern the car, let alone the license plates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 14th, after you learned that Tripkovic had run into difficulties, did you and the men in Kopito ever make an attempt to reach the place where Tripkovic was to see if any of the three men were still alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We didn't move from there. I don't know why. Perica Markovic was probably in charge of all that. He didn't move us from there. He didn't tell us to go anywhere else, so we remained there that night, also, at Kopito.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to your knowledge, no one, not even a scout, went out to try to determine if the three men who had come under attack could be safely reached? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation and assumes facts not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question is "to your knowledge."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to your knowledge, not a single soldier, not even a scout, tried to make their way down to where Tripkovic had been attacked to see if you could reach him, if it was possible to reach him? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. From where we were, no one did. I think it was those from Visegrad who set out. We didn't move from the place where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, if that's true, then no one in your group knows for a fact that the road ahead towards Visegrad is blocked. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, none of us knew. If someone had known, probably something would have been done about it, but we didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you after Djeric comes and tells you that Tripkovic has been attacked between where you are and Visegrad, no one attempts to go and see if they can offer assistance to Tripkovic or the other men. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Object, it's been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it was already answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, but I'm clarifying. He has just said, We didn't know. It seems that he's confused the period of time before he knew about Tripkovic. To be precise, I'm asking him after he learned about Tripkovic, is it true that no one made an attempt to go to these men?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the answer?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you answer that question? After you learned of Trivkovic's attack, did anyone make an attempt to get to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were only told that something was going on down there because the communications had been cut off. We didn't know what it was that was going on down there. We didn't know what had happened to Tripkovic. We only knew that there was something going on and that the communications had been cut off, and then the Visegrad and Rogatica Brigades got in touch with each other, but we did not know what had happened. We didn't know what had happened to Tripkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, now I want the take you to the 15th. You testified that you were told by Goran Djeric that you would go towards the direction of Visegrad on the 15th. When you met up with the soldiers coming from Visegrad, I took from your testimony yesterday that you seemed to meet right at the place where Tripkovic had been attacked. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct. We found those lads from Visegrad. They were already there when we arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between where Kopito and the place where you met the troops from Visegrad, did you encounter any blockages of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 15th, where there any encounters with the enemy? Were any enemy soldiers captured or injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any members of the men either from Kopito or from Visegrad that day, were any of them captured or killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not on that day, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they report, the soldiers from Visegrad, did they report encountering any blockage of the road between Visegrad and the place where you met them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that. I can't say that. They didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection of someone from the group that came up from Visegrad saying to you or saying in your presence that the road had been blocked on their way up? Do you have any recollection of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did they already answer that, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't believe he has, Your Honour. He may have asked and answered on the direct examination but certainly -- on the cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's the answer right before your question, counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You asked: "Did they report, the soldiers from Visegrad, did they report encountering any blockage of the road between Visegrad and the place where you met them?" And he says: "I wouldn't know that. I can't say that. They didn't tell me."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I'm asking Your Honour, did anyone say that in his presence that they didn't tell him directly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anyone from that group in your presence say that they had encountered a blockage in the road between Visegrad and where Tripkovic lay dead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, to recap your evidence with respect to the blockage of the road, on the 13th when you travelled up there, there was no blockage in the road; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you travelled back towards Visegrad on the 15th, there was no blockage in the road; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. We were on our way from up there on foot. The cars were left behind us, and we arrived down there on foot, and there we met up with those lads from Visegrad, and from there we got in our cars and drove to the command at Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, on the 14th, you don't know whether there was a blockage in the road because no one from your group ever made an attempt to try to get to Tripkovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, now, you were asked to comment on a photograph yesterday. I'm going to ask that that photograph be shown to you again. It's P 229. Could I ask that it be placed on the screen. While it's being called up, I want to ask you a couple of questions. The question I want to ask you is, did you recognise these men immediately, or were you prompted in any way with respect to their identities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These people in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we zoom in to the image itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I'm not very clear. Did he recognise them when?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yesterday during his examination-in-chief, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you recognise them immediately, or were you prompted in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised them in the photograph, yesterday and now. After a while, I'm not sure when exactly, these same two men were killed in this car somewhere around Gornja Lijeska. They got blown up by an anti-tank mine, and they were killed on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they present on the 13th of June up in Kopito?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the banner they're carrying? Is that something that the Territorial Defence of the Army of Republika Srpska would carry and display, something like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that. This is not the banner used by the Army of Republika Srpska. They just pick this up somewhere or other, and then they took a photograph, and I don't think I can identify the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we zoom in to the portion of the van just above the flag or the banner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, could I ask you to read what's written in Cyrillic right next to the person that you identified yesterday as Josip.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The lower part of the banner or ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm talking about the painted writing on the front of the van, just above the banner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, it reads: "Josip."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it actually has his name on the van; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's the painted writing on the other side of the van next to the person you identified as Steva, I believe, or Stevan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't see. If we can perhaps zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we take it out of negative image and see if that makes it any more readable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can tell, it reads "Stevan."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's your evidence that you did not need the assistance of what's painted on the van. You had an independent recollection of these men because you knew both of them from that time period; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to show you some other photographs from the same court file in Serbia and ask you, can you help us identify some of these people. The next picture I'd like to you look at is 0644-6678.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, I have to state that these documents were disclosed to us for use in cross-examination at 2.19 this afternoon, after court had started. They were not disclosed to us in compliance with the Court's order that the exhibits for cross-examination were to be given at the time that the witness takes the stand, and I'm just making that for the record since there was such a big deal about when photographs were disclosed yesterday, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is part of the problem with the sparse parsimonious of 65 ters that we get. It was only during the course of his testimony that there was any indication that this man was going to be able to identify these people. I think the Chamber is well aware that it had been the practice of the Prosecution that if for some reason a witness was going to give evidence like that, there would have been a proofing note provided to counsel so they could properly prepare for it. So at the time that I was supposed to advise what documents I was going use in cross-examination, I still had no idea that this man was going to testify that he knew some of the people in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, counsel is saying, Mr. Ivetic, that it arises from the lack of information on the part of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What I will do, is I'm going to allow the questioning, and if you can satisfy me that you're in any way prejudiced, then I'll consider what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour, that's why I said only for the record. Without knowing what questions are going to be asked, I don't know whether I'll be embarrassed, but for the record, I do have to state the reason this wasn't in the 65 ter summary was, again, these photographs given to us by the Prosecutor were not given to us until just recently. So they were not available at the time the 65 ter was made to even know whether any of the witnesses had knowledge of it. This flows from the fact that the Office of the Prosecution disclosed these documents to us in a late manner if.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, not to rehearse the entire disclosure history, but it does bear if a statement like that is going to be made on the record. The file that this is from is 65 ter number 63 from the Milan Lukic Defence exhibit list. It is the judgement from Severin. At the end of last year, the Prosecution notified the Defence that we were in possession of this large file, that we were in the process of reviewing for 66(A)(ii) and 60(A). We also offered to them the opportunity to come look at the documents, to look at the file if they chose. Under 66(B), it's up to them then to ask that they would like us to see photographs, to see these documents. They were available to the Defence. The fact that they did not come and look at them is not something that should prejudice the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I won't respond. I will only say for the record this is not 65 ter from the Milan Lukic list. That is only judgement, the only document we received with respect to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. I've already found a way of resolving the issue, and I've given my ruling. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask that you take a look at 0644-6678, and tell us, do you recognise the person in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We could zoom in on all of these if we could zoom in to the image, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you recognise it to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Milan Lukic, the same man we see over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this photo into evidence as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P 235, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you now to take a look at Exhibit 06 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: A technical matter. Do we know exactly when this photo was taken for purposes of just placement? Accepting the identification of the photo by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's a good point. Could you try and establish that, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the providence of the photographs is dealt with in the Severin judgement. I can ask this witness -- I don't believe that he was present when it was taken, but I can ask him a question that may be helpful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask you, based on the appearance of Milan Lukic, what he's wearing and his age, is this how you remember him in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember him in camouflage uniform with the writing, "police," on the left arm. As for this photograph, I couldn't explain that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking more for your view of his appearances -- your estimation of his age. Thinking back to your recollection of him from the period from 1992 when you had encounters with him, does he appear to be approximately the same age?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't really answer that question specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Could I ask that you take a look at 0644-6596, and these are all photographs from the same series of photographs, and my question will be the same for each of them, whether you recognise anyone. The person I'm interested in you taking a look at is the woman in fatigues on the left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't identify anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Could I ask you to take a look at 0644-6604. Do you recognise this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I ask you, please, to take a look at 0644-6584. Do you recognise this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, we've been provided with a number of documents by the Defence relating to the event that you've testified to. I'm going to show you these documents and ask you whether you recall ever seeing these documents during the time that you served in the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that Defence Exhibit 65 ter 44 be placed on the screen. I can provide the 1D number if that's more helpful. Sorry, that's not the document that I was asking to show. Can I try the 1D number. 1D 22-0175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I had to wait to see which exhibit it was that's coming up. It's the one that I thought it was. The question that's being posed is during the time that you served in the Army of Republika Srpska. This document is clearly not an army document, so I think there has to be foundation laid as to whether this witness has any knowledge of documents that are not from the Army of Republika Srpska. The question implies this would be an army document, but looking at what's coming up on the screen, this is a police document, not an army document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm simply asking the witness whether he'd seen it. Mr. Ivetic led extensive evidence yesterday that police and military engaged in a joint operation on the 13th to the 15th. I'm simply asking this witness, has he seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let him answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Could I ask you to take a look at 65 ter 45, and my question to you is the same. Did you recognise having seen this document related to the Kopito incident before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to take a look at 65 -- Defence 65 ter exhibit 46. That's 1D 22-0179. Ask you, do you recall seeing this document related to the Kopito event prior to today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the documents have been on the screen now that the witness has said he hasn't seen before do not relate to Kopito, so I don't know what documents these are. I don't know if these are the ones Mr. Groome is asking about or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we check -- we have it down as Exhibit 45 from the 65 ter list of the Defence. The 1D number is 1D 22-0177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you have now exceeded the time used by the Defence by about ten minutes. How much longer do you anticipate being?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No more than 15 minutes, Your Honour. I have two important areas of inquiry to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, sir, 1D 22-0179. It's coming up on the screen now, and simply, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, sir. And finally, the last document that I'd like to show you that we were supplied by the Defence in support of what happened in Kopito is Y019-1568. Could I ask you to take a look at this document and tell us whether you recognise this document. Sir, we were not provided with an English translation of this by the Defence, but it is a list of soldiers -- it purports to be a list of soldiers -- police officers sent up to Kopito on the 13th of June, did you see -- have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've never seen this document before. But --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this document was introduced as a Defence exhibit, 1D 25. I want to draw your attention to number 7 on this document. If this document were to be true, it seems that it would contradict your evidence about first seeing Novica Savic up in Kopito. According to this document, he was dispatched from Visegrad up to Kopito on the 13th. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, calls for speculation. I have a further objection, but I don't know if -- I don't want to be accused of lead the witness, but there's other testimony that we've had here before us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You can introduce that. [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Should I finish my objection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. What is it? To rehabilitate the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think the witness has been damaged in any way, but to clarify the objection to the question, as it misstates the evidence as to -- well, again, I don't want to say anything that could be construed as leading evidence -- leading the witness, Your Honour, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Then, please, Your Honour, I'm just asking the witness if the fact that this report causes him to change his answer about seeing Novica Savic up in Kopito and not seeing him in Visegrad town. It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, again, Your Honour, that question implies that there's one Novica Savic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us about the other Novica Savic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There probably is one, since that name's on the list. But what I was saying is that I never had access to any of these lists or documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As for number 7, oh, yeah, there probably is a person like that somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, prior to Mr. Ivetic telling you that there were more than one Novica Savic, did you have personal knowledge of more than one person being named Novica Savic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I did not know a man like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But there probably is one since --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since counsel said there was. I want to show you now your statement from the 7th of April, 2008. It's statement Y018-2198. It's going to be pulled up in front of you, and my question to you is, it seems that it was sworn or notarised on the 7th of April, 2008. Is that correct? Is that your recollection of when you signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was your first meeting with Jelena Rasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think on or about the 7th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you had any prior meeting with her prior to the day you signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any telephone conversation with her where you described your evidence and what you would be able to give evidence about related to the 13th or the 15th of June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We spoke on the phone, but just for me to confirm whether I was willing to see her and whether I was willing to give evidence, so she came to see me at my place on the 7th, and we drew up this record or statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was the 7th of April, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go to have it signed, the official stamp that we see on it? Where was that done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In new Belgrade, the fourth municipal court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender this statement under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P 236 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would also at this time tender a redacted version of the statement. We've removed all of the identifying information from the statement. I would tender that into evidence as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, subject to reviewing the redactions, I would be able to comply, but I can't without having seen the document, know whether all the redactions are satisfactory to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no objections, and we'll do that during the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, now, we were also provided with a statement purporting to be yours taken from you on the 2nd of March, 2008. Now, Mr. Alarid only provided me with the English version and not a Serbian version, so there is no original that I can show you. But I'm going to call up to you the English one, and I want to discuss it with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher to call up Y018-2205, and if the usher could please go to the bottom of the second page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, while we're waiting for the document to be called up, do you read any English at all? If not, I will read the relevant portion to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When it appears on the screen, I'll read the portion I want to draw to your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, this appears to be the draft translation offered by the Defence in compliance with the original deadline for providing the alibi statements at that time only available in B/C/S. Without having the thing on the screen, I can't be certain, but it sounds like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Again, if we could go to the bottom of the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is the draft translation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you go down just a little bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, this document purports to be a statement taken by Jelena Rasic, given by you, and given on the 2nd of March, 2008. That's more than a month prior to the first time you met with Jelena Rasic. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we met on the 7th of April. She took a statement from me, and the next day on the 8th, she came back to see me. We went together to the fourth municipal court, and we got a stamp on that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that from the very first meeting that you had with Jelena Rasic, she was very clear about the testimony she wanted you to give. She knew it prior to asking you what relevant information you had about this case. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how she possibly could have known that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to conclude my examination of you by --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Could I tender this second statement. Again, there's a public version and a redacted -- I'm sorry. We'd ask that the original be tendered under seal, and I have a redacted public version that I would also tender at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, original will become exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have an objection, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. There's an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the problem is by purview of the relevance of this, this becomes at a point in time -- could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a very, very important point. I don't believe I can wrap up in just a couple of questions. I don't know that we have any other witnesses today, and I would ask the indulgence of the Court to give me a little bit of time just to go into what I believe is a very telling piece of evidence here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do we have any other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, Your Honour [microphone not activated]. The Prosecution is correct and we don't object to his extending his time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The question is whether we shouldn't take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Then we could -- sure. It makes sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to conclude with a few questions about your military service. For those in the courtroom that might not be familiar with it, the Yugoslav army prior to the break-up of Yugoslavia required all young men of military age to do mandatory military service, period of about one or two years. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did yours in the 1970s; correct?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified yesterday that you were mobilised into the Territorial Defence of the Army of Republika Srpska; correct? Am I correct in that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, in fact, remembered the date of your mobilisation. You told us it was the 9th of May of 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who issued you your uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they issue you a weapon as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of weapon were you issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a PAP, which is a semi-automatic rifle, and that's what I had. After that, I had a semi-automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- when you were issued your uniform and your weapon, was this all done officially and legally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What rank were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of your commanding officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drago Gavrilovic was the commander of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, again for the benefit of those who may not be intimately familiar with the workings of the Yugoslav People's Army, mobilisation is when the army exercises its legal authority to force men of military age into service. They have no choice. They are forced to serve, and they can be arrested and punished if they refuse to do so. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. Any able-bodied man had to serve in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified that you remained in the Visegrad area until 1996. Did you remain in the Army of the Republika Srpska during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to your job in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had no problems at work. I only had to send them a certificate to my supervisor at work, or when I had time I would go to Belgrade, visit the firm, take along the certificate, and come back, so the certificate had to be submitted at regular intervals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive a salary from the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was very small. When they had money, they would give us something. When they didn't have any, then they didn't. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to read a portion of your testimony yesterday. When you talked about the circumstances surrounding your mobilisation, and it's at transcript 4536, 4536. "Question: Could you tell us the circumstances surrounding your remaining in Bosnia in 1992? "Answer: Yes, it was precisely in those days when they were mobilising people over there. Everyone and I was unable to go back because the roads were blocked, so I stayed and I joined the Territorial Defence." Do you remember being asked that question and giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand where I was asked the question, yesterday here or before when I gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm reading a quote from a question that Mr. Ivetic put to you yesterday afternoon sometime around this time. I'll read it to you again. He said: "Could you tell us the circumstances surrounding your remaining in Bosnia in 1992?" And your answer was: "Yes, it was precisely in those days that they were mobilising people over there, everyone, and I was unable to go back because the roads were blocked, so I stayed and I joined the Territorial Defence." Do you recall giving that answer yesterday to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, is it your evidence that the road between Visegrad and Belgrade was blocked? It was impassable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There was a place called Vardiste where it was blocked, and able-bodied men could not leave in the direction of Serbia unless they had a special certificate from the army or the SUP, so regardless of the fact that I had my residence in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, if I understand what you meant when you said "blocked" yesterday, you meant that there was a check-point there, and they were checking men of military age to make sure that they were not leaving the area but that they were mobilised into the military. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, but you used the word, "I joined the Territorial Defence ..." So my question to you is, were you mobilised, forced into the Territorial Defence, or did you voluntarily join the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they started collecting people, rounding them up in the villages, all that was left for me to do was flee through the woods to Serbia or be mobilised together with all the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember when you were -- when you left the Army of the Republika Srpska? As close to a date as you're able to give us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In April 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, MLD4, when your name was provided to us as a witness and we saw in your statement saying that you served in the Army of Republika Srpska, we sent a request to the government of Republika Srpska to ask them to check their records about your military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that Exhibit 0645-8677 be placed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to now show you what they say about your military service. The report that you will see on the screen is the official document we received from the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I just ask the Prosecution to state when they disclosed this document, and I don't think we've seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Under what rule should I have disclosed this, Your Honour? It was provided to the Defence yesterday when we were required to disclose documents that we're going to use on cross-examination. If Mr. Alarid is suggesting that there's an earlier date that it should have been disclosed, I appreciate to know under what rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is the Chamber directing me to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the point of the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, simply put, [microphone not activated] [Previous translation continues]... we received it yesterday, I guess, according to that, and I'd just like to know when they received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't see the relevance of that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's fine, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's when you received it that's important, from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so that the record is complete, Mr. Van Hooydonk informs me that we received it on the 19th of January and we disclosed it on the 19th of January, the same day that we received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: MLD4, there's absolutely no record in the custody of the Republika Srpska government of you ever having been mobilised or volunteered or having served in any capacity in any unit at any time with the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, without knowing what was requested of the government of Republika Srpska, I believe that Mr. Groome's grandiose statement is lacking foundation. All we have is this response. It doesn't say what was asked of the authorities of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm entitled to put it to the witness. I will be seeking to mark this for identification and will supply the Chamber with the request and the full response in a written motion when I seek its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I believe you're entitled to put it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please answer. You have your hand up. Please explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What you are saying that in 1978 I was no longer registered in Visegrad, that's probably true, but I was registered in Zemun because I lived in Surcin. Surcin belongs to Zemun municipality. After that, I moved my address to new Belgrade, so I belonged to new Belgrade municipality. As for the documents you asked for from the government of Republika Srpska, I can show you my military booklet with stamps in it from the Army of Republika Srpska showing what time I spent there, and I have this military booklet with the stamps in it with me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, are you willing to allow us to place it in evidence in this trial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have Mr. -- Mr. Ivetic first, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Only a matter that since we are in open session, the part at page 6, lines 3 through 5, ought to be redacted because that could lead someone to conclude the identity. I just rose because I don't know what the time limit is for the redactions to take place for the live feed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any objection to your military booklet being placed in evidence in this trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have it with me with the stamps in it, and you can look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you need the original for any pension or anything you receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to keep it. I brought my military booklet with me, but I have to keep it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps if you would allow the usher to have it for a short time, then I will work with the counsel on Milan Defence team about how we might document it, either by taking photographs of it or photocopying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No objection to either way, whatever is easiest for the court to put into evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it your evidence that your military records are located in the Republic of Serbia in Zemun?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My military file is in new Belgrade because my place of residence is now new Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that if we ask in new Belgrade to see your military file, we will find -- it will corroborate the dates that you've given us as you were being a member of the Army of Republika Srpska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, yes. Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's be clear. You were one of five Defence witnesses that we made the request at the same time to the Republika Srpska, and out of the five, the government checked their records and supplied us with the dates of their military service in Visegrad. They supplied us with the dates of three of the people of the military service. It was just you and one other person who has no record. They have no record of. I'd ask you to take a look at paragraph 1, and would you read that for us. Paragraph 1 on the screen in front of you, sir. Could you read paragraph 1 on the monitor in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would object to this. The witness didn't generate this document. I think it would be improper for him to read it. He's already asked and answered the questions with regards to his military service and provided the relevant booklet. The offer of the Prosecutor to have him read this document which he did not generate and we have not had any real foundation for is otherwise simply self-serving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I don't see the point in his reading it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask a follow-up question with respect to the person who's listed in paragraph, someone who he's testified he knows quite well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Am I allowed to ask him to read that first paragraph? Just a few words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, what is the follow-up question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Whether he knows whether Goran Djeric was, in fact, a member of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you can ask him that and then refer him to the -- you can ask him that and refer him to what is in the first. Is that number 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified yesterday that you knew Goran Djeric, I believe you said, quite well. Was he a member, to your knowledge, of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was, but he was in the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I ask you to read the first paragraph on the document in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand what I should answer, what the question is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, can you simply read the paragraph there in front of you. What follows numeral I?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Djeric, son of Ilija, Goran, is not in our records ."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my final question to you is, if you and Mr. Djeric were not official members of the Army of Republika Srpska, would you have -- were you a member of Milan Lukic's paramilitary group?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: He's got two questions here. The first question -- sorry, compound question. The first question misstates the evidence. His testimony has been that he was a member. As for the other one, let him ask it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please break the questions down, Mr. Groome.
