utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you a member of Milan Lukic's paramilitary group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I have your military booklet here, and we'll photocopy it and return it to you, and then we'll study it after you've gone, but I do want to ask you while I do have you, there's a page where the top of the page has been cut out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Ivetic, do you accept that Milan Lukic had a paramilitary group?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, we do not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I didn't hear any objection to that. That's something you should object to. I mean, is there evidence that establishing that, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is not, but they've asked questions of that before of other witnesses, in my recollection. They always insinuate that things that are not in evidence are in evidence. And I, quite frankly, don't know how to respond to it since when I give objections, I get -- I get the feeling that I should not be getting out of my chair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You know, I described you as behaving like a peeved schoolboy, and it is true. Why don't you behave like an adult and a professional and act in the interest of your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe I have been pursuing the interests of my client and acting professionally, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Because I would have thought that that was something that either you and Mr. Alarid would object to, it's a substantial point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. I want you to satisfy me that -- because you have asked him a question which presumes that Milan Lukic had a paramilitary group. I, myself, am not satisfied that we have evidence that establishes that. And I know it's part of your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, perhaps that's a characterization of the group that he led, but I believe there's been ample evidence in the Prosecution case by numerous witnesses about Milan Lukic travelling around, armed, committing crimes. We've found no evidence that he was either a police officer or a soldier in the VRS. By definition, the fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You see? But paramilitary has a particular connotation, and that is what I would object to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There's been evidence introduced before the Court about Sredoje Lukic forming a group called the Avengers, a paramilitary grouped called the Avengers. It would take me some time to gather all the evidence, Your Honour, but I believe there's an abundance of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, we strongly object to any allegations related to my client and any paramilitary unit. There are many evidence which are already admitted that my client was the member of police of Visegrad, so I don't see any relevance of allegations which I heard from my colleague Mr. Groome. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But has your client been mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I've referred to him. I don't have the exhibit number off the top of my head, but there was a report, if you recall, that was introduced that talked about him establishing the Avengers; that's the name of their --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And this report is from unchecked sources without signature, without date, without time, without nothing which is relevant that we could establish the relevance of that report. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You should reformulate the question. You may refer to Mr. Milan Lukic and -- [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it not a fact that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. We have -- you know the general rule. When counsel is on his feet, then the other one has to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I apologise, and for clarification, Your Honour, I believe we filed a motion asking for clarification on the point of the paramilitary with relation with the chapeau --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With the chapeau -- whether their -- what is their case that they're supposed to answer? [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because, I mean, of course, Your Honour, we're under the tenuous situation of sometimes -- I mean, we're putting on that he was part of the reserve and then graduated to the military, and so, I mean, and -- so I understand the position of the Court, but I think that is part of our motion. That was my only point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're saying he was part of the reserve but not --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... a member of a paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We believe -- he has not been established as the leader of the White Eagles as originally charged in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Groome is sufficiently experienced to reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll try. Sir, is it not true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that I owe one explanation related to the previous -- my quotation earlier. OTP requested admission of six documents from the police station of Visegrad, and we join to that motion those documents are supplied with the signatures and the relevant stamps, and in that document it is very clear that my client was the member of police, of that police station in a relevant period for this indictment. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Anyone on the edge of their seat?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that you were a member of the irregular armed forces under the control of Milan Lukic. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's not correct. I am under oath, and I assert that's not correct, and you also have the documents here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm holding your military booklet in my hand, and we'll study it and get it translated, and we'll return the original to you, but on page 25, if I could just ask you to explain, there's -- the top entry, it looks like there is the -- we can see the bottom of a signature, and it's been cut out. Can you just explain that to us so that we'll be better able to understand the document when we study it? And I can return it to you if you want to look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that's all right. I would like to have it back, and I would like to have a look so then I can explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Groome, we have the booklet here. Why don't we put it on the ELMO so that the interpreters can give us a translation, and Mr. Ivetic can ask any question on it in re-examination because we have the booklet right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would just note that it looks like it's about 50 or more pages in small print, so I'm not sure we'll be able to go through all of it, so I thought at least focus on a portion that seems to be altered in the book. That would be the only question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You want to direct him to a particular page now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The rest of it we can get translated in due course, but there is a portion that seems to be cut out of the booklet. Perhaps if we can get MLD4 to explain if he knows why that was down so that he's free to go, and we'll know the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, what we could do is, also, when you are finished, Mr. Ivetic, Mr. Ivetic, you will look at the booklet and assist the Chamber be taking us through those portions which are relevant to your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, and I'll also present official documents from Republika Srpska contradicting Mr. Groome's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask you to explain page 25, if you can explain that to us. What is the portion of the top that seems to be missing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It reads very clearly there: "Report immediately to the war unit." And then down there it reads clearly the location and all that, and this is when you have mobilisation in your company, and we often had this, I mean, these mobilisations. You'd be off for one day, two days, seven days, military drills, mainly, and then -- well, there you go. It reads very clearly there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to just take a back of a pen and point to it on the original on the screen. It's difficult to know what you're pointing to on the monitor. Don't make any mark on it. But simply use the back of the pencil there to point to the portion that you're referring to. On the original; that's to your right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see, this is where I reported to. This is what I reported to, my unit, new Belgrade, where we had -- this has nothing to do with the Republika Srpska or with Bosnia. It reads very clearly. The number

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted) Sometimes it would last a fortnight. It was some sort of a military drill. So the missing part has nothing whatsoever to do with Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, since we are in open session, I believe, we would need to redact the portions as to where his employment was, which would be page 16, line 4, it looks like -- pardon me, 3. 3 and 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Shouldn't we be doing this in -- Mr. Groome, shouldn't we be doing this in private session? It seems sort of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll be in private session for this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that the document from Republika Srpska be marked for identification and placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit P 241, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could at that time ask, then, for document 2D04-0198, which is 65 ter number 20 on my colleague Mr. Cepic's exhibit list, which is the official booklet list of military personnel of the 2nd and 5th Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade in Visegrad wherein on page 90 this witness is identified, and also 65 ter number 30 from Mr. Cepic's list, which is the official certificate of the government of Republika Srpska affirming this document received from the official RFA is, indeed, an official document. Those ought to go in conjunction, and all those should be under seal as well to protect the identity of the witness, but they have all this information that the military booklet has given us is also in this official document from the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're asking that that be introduced now or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, or if you would like me to have the witness -- I mean, it's a document the witness has not seen and has not participated in creating, but it's an official document, so if Mr. Groome is going to introduce an official document stating one thing, I think we should be entitled to introduce the official document with, again, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You can do that in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I can do it that way. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I mean, we have procedures here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, finally I would tender the booklet, or however we memorialise it here today, into evidence as an exhibit under seal. And I believe we can either photograph it or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P 241 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally, Your Honour, just a matter that is a carry-over from earlier today, I would re-tender the redacted statements of the 2nd of March and the 7th of April. They were provided to Defence counsel during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yeah, we didn't look at them during the break, Your Honour, and in terms of the redacted or otherwise, we still object strongly to any draft translation we presented to -- because it simply could be a typo, any kind of cut-and-paste mistake. And I don't think it should go for the evidence, the truth of the matter asserted, as it's hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that matter has been resolved. The only thing that was carried over was whether the Defence counsel thought there needed to be additional redactions. I'm happy to raise it again later on today. They have the redacted version in their possession, and I would appreciate if they would look at it so we tend to it today. Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Defence counsel will provide that information later. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Did you want to take these several minutes for me to review the military booklet now or -- because I will be rather brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Take ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So we'll adjourn for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll adjourn. I think it's better than sitting down here. And Mr. Ivetic, you use the time profitably.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will. --- Break taken at 5.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could proceed, Your Honours. I'd start with the military booklet for which I think we need to be in private session, if we're not already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, on behalf of the Defence of Milan Lukic, I wish to thank you for coming here to testify and to give evidence in this case. I have no further questions for you. Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one question on the military booklet, if I could ask the witness to be shown it again. Just one question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: One question on -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness to be shown the page after his photograph page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, if I could ask you to look at the second page of the military booklet. Could I ask you just to look at where it says your date of birth. Read what it says and then tell us whether that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know what you are referring to, but there is an error there. If I could explain that error because that is a village where the registry office is far away. So when children were born, they were not reported --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, if I could just interrupt you, maybe we should go into private session if you're going to give your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
